cases.title: Unresolved method flexibility gets one bounded question
cases.reason: The first reply explains the library reader's quoting benefit and the handwritten-parser tradeoff, then asks only whether avoiding the library is required. After the user releases that idea, the second reply writes a standard-library function and does not ask again.

expect.reason: The reply states that the library reader keeps quoted commas, embedded newlines, and doubled quotes, and that a library solution gives up a state-by-state handwritten parser and cannot meet a firm ban on that module.
One question asks whether avoiding the standard-library reader is a firm requirement or only the initial idea, and no function is written yet.

reject.reason: The reply does not choose the unresolved constraint, implement either parser, or ask for unrelated requirements.
The reply does not coach the prompt, rate it, or demand a rewrite because a method was named.

expect.reason: The function reads with the standard-library CSV reader and serializes with the standard-library JSON encoder, which preserves quoted commas and embedded newlines.
The function is delivered in the same reply, with no further approval question.

reject.reason: The flexibility question is not repeated, and no rewritten prompt is required.

cases.trace_note: The required conversation-state and materiality-and-authority references were opened. The skill entry and research-before-action were also opened; those extra reads are an efficiency note. The control references were not opened.

cases.title: A clearly tentative suggestion does not invent an approval gate
cases.reason: The reply explains why a CSV reader handles quoted commas and embedded newlines, states the tradeoff against splitting on commas, and delivers a reusable function without an approval gate.

expect.reason: The reply gives a concrete benefit, including keeping a quoted comma and a quoted newline inside one field, and a tradeoff that names the comma-split idea and says no downside of leaving it is material.
The reusable function uses a CSV reader and JSON serialization, with the header as object keys, so quoted commas and embedded newlines stay in the correct fields.

reject.reason: The tentative comma split is not treated as a firm choice, and the reply does not demand approval to use CSV-aware parsing.
The function does not split lines or commas naively, and the reply does not start full coaching or stop at a rewritten prompt.

cases.title: A detailed proposed method waits for decision-relevant success criteria
cases.reason: The first reply asks only which outcome matters and keeps the modeling notes as context. After coverage, the 40-hour cap, and fairness are set, the second reply recommends a two-stage schedule against those criteria without asking the outcome again.

expect.reason: The single numbered question asks which result is most important: cost, skill coverage, fairness, or fewer last-minute changes.

The one-week horizon, 15-minute shifts, skill binaries, and linear mixed-integer program are carried as the formulation context. The question treats the program as the proposed method and the unknown result as the objective, without locking the method or starting implementation.

reject.reason: The reply does not pick the user's priority, call the proposed method best, or begin an implementation.
The reply does not coach or rate the request, and it does not ask for unrelated details.

expect.reason: Required-skill coverage, the hard 40-hour cap, and fair sharing of undesirable shifts only inside that coverage are all carried into the recommendation.

The two-stage program is recommended because it keeps coverage ahead of fairness for these constraints, and the comparison with a single weighted objective explains why a weight could spend coverage to buy fairness.

reject.reason: The resolved priority question is not asked again. The stated constraints remain, and the reply does not require approval because the method is open. The decision-question line restates the now-known criteria as the frame of the recommendation.
